BOOTSTRAP from empty (the genuine build path). An empty tree + 3 tileable observed windows (ids 1,2,3) + focused_leaf:null on a single WIDE display (usable union = {x:0,y:0,w:1200,h:800}). sync builds the scaffold (root region → d:1 pinned mount, since all 3 windows home to display 1) then chains 3 BSP adopts inside the mount, id-sorted, re-projecting the growing tree between each so every split reads its target leaf's CURRENT frame. The mount projects onto the full usable rect, so per-display sub-frames equal the old whole-canvas frames here. ORIENTATION DERIVATION (split_orientation: w>=h → row, else col):
  • adopt w:1: empty mount → SEED the mount child = [w:1]. anchor := w:1.
  • adopt w:2: project → w:1 is the mount's lone leaf, frame = full 1200x800 → w>=h → ROW. mount child becomes i:w:2(row)=[w:1, w:2]. anchor := w:2.
  • adopt w:3: project → i:w:2 row splits the 1200-wide mount into two 600x800 halves; w:2 (right child) frame = {x:600,y:0,w:600,h:800} → 600<800 → COL. w:2 replaced in i:w:2's slot by i:w:3(col)=[w:2,w:3]. anchor := w:3.
Final: root → d:1 → i:w:2(row)=[w:1, i:w:3]; i:w:3(col)=[w:2,w:3]. The alternating row→col is the load-bearing proof that each split sees its target's REAL projected frame inside the mount, not the static canvas. auto_proportion leaves the computed nodes ratio-free, and the empty-input case exercises ensure_scaffold's fresh build + the per-mount adopt seeding/chaining.
